method: Every expectation was written from the sources by reading them. No analysis tool was run on them, and no tool's detectors, source code or output were looked at. Line numbers were looked up by a scratch script that finds the line of a given piece of text and fails unless it occurs exactly once. A second scratch script ran main.js and both preloads in Node against a stand-in for the electron module (and for node:https and node:fs) and printed every ipcMain registration, webContents.send, new BrowserWindow with its merged webPreferences, request (fetch, https.get, net.request), file access, and the channel each exposed member invokes, sends on or listens to, with file:line; its output agreed with the expectations. The renderers were checked by reading only. LANGUAGE: main.js, both preloads and the modules in main/, common/ and preload/ are CommonJS in the shape tsc emits ("use strict", exports.X = ..., enums compiled to an IIFE over Channel, imported functions called as (0, mod_1.fn)(...)); renderer.js, renderer-flasher.js and renderer-diagnostics.js are ES modules, and renderer.js imports renderer/*.js. FILE ATTRIBUTION (as in holdout5): facts are attributed to the source file a reader sees them in. Receivers of table channels name main/ipc-table.js (the table and the loop that calls ipcMain.handle / ipcMain.on are both there). Senders and receivers that go through the IpcClient class name preload.js, where the channel is handed to the client; the ipcRenderer calls themselves are in preload/ipc-client.js (the places lists give both). flash:progress is sent from main/flash-session.js. Every window is created in main/windows.js. In the bundled and minified inputs the modules are bundled into their entry file; bundledFiles maps each module to that file, and line numbers then do not apply. Channel names come from the compiled TypeScript enum Channel (common/ipc-contract.js), from constants exported by other modules (main/flash-session.js FLASH_START, main/telemetry.js TELEMETRY_CHANNEL) and from literals; all are resolvable by evaluating the source, and no channel name is computed at run time. webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration, sandbox, one entry per window and key the code writes (also through SECURE_DEFAULTS and the helper prefsFor); window names the module variable that holds the window; count in an absent entry is one more than the number of windows that have that value, as in holdout4/holdout5. IPC payloads are not a scored class; the object literals sent over IPC are listed under ipcPayloadsUnscored for a reader, and nothing reads them. For this case the sources are padwright/src with changes.json applied the way derive() in corpus/build.mjs applies it (its edits, then prependCommentLines: 3 comment lines in front of every .js file, so every fact moves down at least 3 lines). The harness was run on that derived tree as well. changes lists what differs from padwright (plain), in the spelling of holdout5; unchangedMoves lists facts that only moved to another line and must not be reported as changes. The new payload field (dryRun in keymap:write) is listed under changes.ipcPayloadsUnscored and is not scored.

present.why: Channel.ListDevices = "device:list" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.ListDevices, kind: "handle", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.handle(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. Sender: preload.js member listDevices, client.invoke(ipc_contract_1.Channel.ListDevices, ...) on the IpcClient of preload/ipc-client.js, whose invoke calls ipcRenderer?.invoke(channel, payload). Returns bus.list().

Channel.OpenFlasher = "flasher:open" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.OpenFlasher, kind: "on", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.on(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. Sender: preload.js member openFlasher, client.send(ipc_contract_1.Channel.OpenFlasher, ...) on the IpcClient of preload/ipc-client.js, whose send calls ipcRenderer?.send(channel, payload). Fire and forget: kind "on" in the table, client.send in the preload. Opens the flasher window.
